working_title: Replay QA: Bugs That Only Exist in Time
audience: Engineering leads, front-end developers and teams shipping web apps with AI coding agents who want end-to-end QA without writing or maintaining browser tests; a ~90 s product promo, so every claim must be a capability or an exact number they can check in the product or docs.
central_questions: What exactly does Replay QA do when you point it at a URL, and what does 'fully managed end-to-end testing' mean in its own vocabulary (projects, explorations, journeys, test runs, bugs, polish passes, versions, recordings)?

How does Replay QA keep testing without a human: environment schedules, staging/production/preview/local environments, main-branch deployments and every pull request, with results posted back to GitHub and bugs filed to trackers?

Why are some bugs (polling loops, re-fetch storms, long React commits that drop frames) only provable with a time-travel recording of the runtime, and what are the exact numbers in the account's featured bugs?
What does a Replay QA bug report contain (root cause, causal chain, evidence, severity, status) and how is a fix verified, and what do the account's Insights totals show?
How do coding agents drive the same loop (llms.txt, REST API, MCP, Replay MCP on a recording), which grounds the subtle developer-agent / critic-agent beat?

topics.title: Bugs that only exist in time: runtime replay, network and React polish passes

What are the exact numbers in each featured bug (67 ms commit at T=383.2s, 4 dropped frames, 25 of 27 fibers wasted, ~34 ms waste, 16.7 ms frame budget; 56 ms commit, 87 fibers, 3 dropped frames; 258 re-fetches, checkpoint -1, ~631 ms avg; 105 identical empty responses every ~800 ms, waitMs=500 vs 10000)?
What do the bug-react and bug-sync takes show on screen at each mark (bug-react report 3032, actual 8723, rootcause 12008 ms; bug-sync report 1603, actual 5402, rootcause 8154 ms)?
Which featured bugs are open vs fixed, and which product does each come from (the 67 ms and 56 ms bugs are on Replay QA's own Projects page; the 258 and 105 bugs are on a 'reading-room' app)?
